messages:
maya (Support): Heads-up — support inbox is getting a few escalations: p95s jumped ~2.5x and p99s ~3x for late-night customers after yesterday's runtime rollout. Two customers (ACME, Nimbus) hit timeouts.
lewis (Eng Oncall): Thanks Maya. Any correlation with deploys? Can you paste an example request id or a short trace?
maya (Support): ACME request id: acme-req-9f2, Nimbus request id: nimbus-42a. Quick log lines below from their uploads:
```
[2026-03-14T03:14:22Z] req=acme-req-9f2 path=/v1/generate latency_ms=1280 kernel=latebind queue_ms=940 host=rt-13
[2026-03-14T03:15:01Z] req=nimbus-42a path=/v1/embed latency_ms=1422 kernel=latebind auth_refresh=1
```
lewis (Eng Oncall): Noted. I see a canary deploy completed around 03:12 UTC. @deploy-bot posted the rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime-service v2.3.0 -> v2.3.1 (canary 10% -> 100%) by ci/cd-pipeline ✅
priya (Runtime): I’m looking at the canary traces now. Canary metric jump aligns with kernel scheduler change landed in v2.3.1 — the new latebind heuristic + slightly changed prefetch window. Initial hypothesis: higher queueing on certain tenants triggering tail latency. Also saw a few auth refreshes at the same time (auth service returned 503 briefly).
tom (SRE): Two possible contributors: (1) scheduling bump -> more work on slow-path, (2) concurrent auth-refresh causing synchronous token fetch which blocks request path. Logs show `auth_refresh=1` paired with long queue_ms.
lewis (Eng Oncall): Can we reproduce locally with a cohort? Maya, can we get a repro: sample payload sizes, model (gpt-XXXX), and whether ACME uses dedicated routing?
maya (Support): ACME uses hosted default route, model=gpt-13k, typical seq_len ~1024. Smallish batch sizes. I'll DM the sample payloads and tokens.
priya (Runtime): Repro plan: run sustained ramp with sequence length distro 512-2048, enable latebind on a canary host, and simulate auth refresh storms (drop auth cache for one tenant). Quick repro script (run on perf lab):
```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..2000}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: acme" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-13k","input":"a" * 700}' https://perf-rt.local/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
priya (Runtime): Early local runs reproduced p95 jump when auth cache was cleared and latebind heuristics were active. Queueing time rose from ~30ms -> 900ms on hot hosts.
lewis (Eng Oncall): OK. Short-term mitigation options? revert scheduler heuristic, rollback runtime, or put an auth-cache grace to avoid synchronous fetch.
priya (Runtime): Fastest: flip feature-flag to disable new scheduler heuristic (can be toggled per-cluster) and re-run canary. If that removes spike we plan rollback. Medium: patch auth path to async refresh so it doesn't block token validation (needs small code change).
tom (SRE): We should also roll back customer-facing routes for the most-impacted tenants to older runtime pool (routing rule) as an immediate relief while we bisect. Can we do tenant pinning?
lewis (Eng Oncall): Yes, traffic-split API supports pinning tenants to legacy runtime group for now. Maya — can you collect the list of tenants affected and percent traffic?
maya (Support): ACME and Nimbus are 2 largest, others with spikes: PingLabs, Helix. I’ll compile and DM counts.
priya (Runtime): Quick command to toggle heuristic flag on the control plane:
```
redwoodctl runtime feature-toggle set scheduler_latebind_heuristic=false --cluster=prod-us-east
```
priya (Runtime): If someone can flip the flag on a single canary host, we can validate in 10min. If p95 falls we plan to roll the flag cluster-wide and then schedule a formal rollback for v2.3.1.
lewis (Eng Oncall): I’ll flip on one canary host now and watch graphs. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/latency/rt-tail?orgId=1
(lewis did :eyes: reaction)
lewis (Eng Oncall): Flip done on canary host rt-13. Early numbers: p95 decreased from 720ms -> 210ms within 60s on that host. p99 still noisy but trending down.
priya (Runtime): That strongly implicates the scheduler heuristic. I recommend rolling the flag across cluster and schedule a rollback of v2.3.1 if the flag flip does not fully resolve tail.
tom (SRE): I'll also open a short-lived routing pin for ACME and Nimbus to legacy runtime pool until the flag is cluster-wide.
lewis (Eng Oncall): Timeline proposal: now — flip flag cluster-wide (20m), validate p95/p99 for 30m, then decide rollback. If flag resolves, no rollback needed, but we still need root-cause PR to adjust heuristic and async auth refresh.
maya (Support): I'll notify customers (ACME, Nimbus) of mitigations and expected ETA ~45m.
priya (Runtime): Postmortem action items: 1) add canary workload that exercises auth-refresh path + long sequences to deployment tests, 2) add perf gate for tail-latency delta > 20% in canary window, 3) make auth refresh async by default.
lewis (Eng Oncall): Good. Running mitigations now. Keep thread updated with any customer hits.
maya (Support): Thanks team — updating customers now.
priya (Runtime): flag set cluster-wide. Monitoring.
lewis (Eng Oncall): p95 cluster-wide back to baseline, p99 improving. Closing escalation once customers confirm.
maya (Support): ACME replied: "latency looks normal now, thanks." :white_check_mark:
lewis (Eng Oncall): Great job. We'll keep the feature-flagged heuristic disabled until we ship the corrected scheduler PR and auth async fix.
priya (Runtime): Will open PRs and link here.
lewis (Eng Oncall): End of thread — add any follow-ups as replies.
